title: Essential: spacecraft-frame distance
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly compute the distance to Earth at reflection as measured in the spacecraft frame, obtaining 9.0 × 10⁹ m.

title: Essential: Earth-frame distance
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly compute the distance to the spacecraft at signal reception as measured in the Earth frame, obtaining 2.7 × 10¹⁰ m.

title: Important: spacecraft-frame symmetry
description: Important Criteria: The student must recognize that in the spacecraft frame, the one-way travel time of the signal to Earth is half the total round-trip time (30 s).

title: Important: Earth-frame time dilation
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply time dilation to find the Earth-frame duration for the round trip (100 s) from the spacecraft's proper time (60 s).

title: Important: Earth-frame kinematics setup
description: Important Criteria: The student must set up the correct simultaneous equations relating the Earth-frame distances at emission and reception using the total light path and the spacecraft's displacement.

title: Optional: unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The student demonstrates consistent use of SI units (meters, seconds) and the speed of light throughout the calculation.

title: Pitfall: frame confusion
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student mixes measurements from different frames (e.g., using Earth-frame time in a spacecraft-frame distance calculation) without proper transformation.

title: Pitfall: neglecting relativity
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student treats the problem with classical kinematics, ignoring time dilation or the constancy of the speed of light.
